answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with bonded identity plus random audits. Each worker posts a bond and earns reputation through signed attestations, so minting fake agents demands fresh capital but grants no inherited trust. At epoch close a verifier issues a cipher challenge; agents whose answers diverge across a cluster have their bond slashed. Reward is a nectar of fees paid only to stakes that survive audit, while a marble ledger records each slash. Every fake identity needs its own bond and risks the slash, so the attacker's cost grows while influence stays capped.
